one_month_reasoning: The one scheduled company event in the window is Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-14. Guidance is sales EUR 11-12B and GM 55-57%; consensus is EUR 10.65 EPS on EUR 11.68B sales (in euros; my round-1 '$12.54 on $13.2B' was a bad conversion). H1 sales were EUR 18.1B, so the EUR 43-45B FY guide needs EUR 25-27B in H2, and the print itself should be fine. The stock reaction will hinge on first 2027 colour, 2028 order intake and whether H2 cash conversion recovers (H1 FCF was about EUR -1.3B as receivables rose to EUR 7.8B), which is the one skeptic item that could surprise on the downside on the day. Round 1 had NDAA/MATCH headlines as a possible in-window downside skew; that was wrong. The Senate adjourned 2026-09-30 and returns the week of 11-09, and the expected path is a December compromise text, so a MATCH outcome inside the window is essentially ruled out. The FOMC meets 10-27/28 after the 09-16 hike; markets lean to no change in October with a December hike priced, so it is a modest risk. Hyperscaler Q3 capex updates in late October skew slightly up. Net: no directional tilt. The stock has rebounded about 15% from the 2026-09-14 close of $1,575.15. I centre on spot with a 1-month sigma of about 13.5% (46%/3.5, nudged up for earnings day; ASML's October moves have ranged widely around prints), with tails a touch wider than round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of (a) 28x NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of $64.7 (25% FY2027 EUR 50.9, 75% FY2028 EUR 59.8, at EUR/USD 1.1243) = $1,812 (55%); (b) 2026-28 average EPS of $56.0 x 32x through-cycle P/E = $1,792 (20%); (c) a 3.0% yield on 2028E FCF of EUR 18.9B ($21.3B) over 376M shares = $1,884 (25%). Blended fair value about $1,825, roughly 1% above spot.

EUR 61B x 36.5% (slight opex leverage) / 372M = EUR 59.8. Consensus range EUR 53.1 (ChartMill, stale) to 68.3 (MarketScreener); Bernstein EUR 67. Round 1's EUR 55 implied a ~32% margin on consensus sales, which I cannot justify, so I lift it as the supervisor found.

Today ~31x CY2027 / ~33x blended NTM; 15-year average P/E 34.4x; NTM EV/EBITDA 23.6x vs 10-year mean 24.9x (Torre). 28x is ~5 turns of de-rating because in Oct-2027 the market will be pricing 2028-29, the window in which semicap upcycles have historically ended, and the Fed's 2026-09-16 hike to 3.75-4.00% (another priced for December) argues against holding the historical average. I do not cut further: the hike supports the de-rating already assumed.

bear.story: The MATCH Act rides the December NDAA compromise text (which does not need a Senate floor vote) with DUV immersion and servicing bans on SMIC, Huawei, Hua Hong, CXMT and YMTC; the 150-day ally clock brings unilateral FDPR controls around mid-2027. At the same time financing-dependent hyperscalers pace 2027-28 capex, Korean memory makers (43% of Q2 system sales) digest their HBM build, 2028 EUV slots are pushed out, and the H1 receivables build turns out to be a sign of stretched customers rather than timing. 2028 EPS stalls near EUR 48 ($54) and the market pays ~21x for a late-cycle cyclical with a hiking Fed.

base.story: 2027 revenue about EUR 53.5B (+22%) and EPS about EUR 51; 2028 guided to mid-teens growth (EPS about EUR 60). MATCH passes in some form in December but with the ally window and service carve-outs, so the hit is a few percent of 2028. Cash conversion recovers in H2-26. The multiple compresses from ~33x NTM to ~28-29x, so EPS growth roughly offsets de-rating.

bull.story: AI and DRAM demand pull the 2028 plan to 110+ EUV units, Zeiss keeps pace, EUV price increases stick and GM reaches 58-60%; MATCH is stripped or diluted in the four-corners text. 2028 EPS reaches consensus/Bernstein levels of ~EUR 68 ($76.5) at ~34-35x.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $1,200 (-34%, roughly a 1-sigma annual move, ~21x 2027E EPS of $57.3 and well under the $1,575.15 close of 2026-09-14, the AI-pacing panic low) the market would be pricing falling earnings, not just multiple compression on growing earnings. Most likely causes: customers pushing out 2027/2028 EUV slots (bookings collapse, 2028 capacity plan withdrawn), a MATCH Act enacted with an immediate servicing ban on the China installed base, or the H1 receivables build turning into write-downs. Unchanged level; reference low corrected.

reasoning: Second round, skeptic lane. The supervisor's fact-checks exposed three errors in my round 1: (1) the NDAA timeline came from an FY26 note; the FY27 House bill passed 2026-07-22, Senate cloture failed 07-14, the Senate is out until the week of 11-09 and a December four-corners text is the path (CRS IN12704, ndaa.ai, Breaking Defense; verified). That moves MATCH risk out of the 1-month window and into December, but a compromise text that bypasses the Senate floor keeps enactment odds near my prior (~50%). (2) The Q3 consensus is EUR 10.65 on EUR 11.68B, not a USD figure. (3) My 2028 EPS of EUR 55 sat below the ~EUR 65B revenue consensus (MarketScreener: EPS EUR 68.3; verified) and my separate 15% cycle-normalization leg counted the same downturn twice. I accept (3) in part: I lifted 2027 revenue to EUR 53.5B and 2028 to EUR 61B (still ~6% below consensus for optics limits and expected MATCH cost) giving EPS EUR 50.9 / 59.8, and replaced the haircut leg with a 2026-28 average EPS at a rate-adjusted 32x. I disagree with treating consensus as the base without a haircut: the 2028 plan is 'under review' and the consensus range (EUR 53-68) is wide. New skeptic evidence I added: H1-26 FCF was about EUR -1.3B as receivables rose to EUR 7.8B, and consensus FCF conversion is only 63% (2026) and 86% (2027), so my round-1 assumption FCF = net income was too generous; the FCF leg now uses 85% conversion on 2028 NI. I also added the Fed's 2026-09-16 hike to 3.75-4.00% (CNBC; Polymarket ~81% another 2026 hike), which I use to hold the horizon multiple at 28x and trim the through-cycle P/E, not to cut further. Credit (Moody's A1 positive, S&P A+), litigation (class action in discovery), insiders (no red flags) and short interest (~0.4%) are unchanged and give no bear signal. Fair value rises from $1,700 to about $1,825; the scenario mean is about $1,875. The 12-month ladder uses a median of about $1,820 with a lognormal sigma of ~44% below and ~40% above the median (backlog visibility trims the upside vol; policy/cycle fatten the left tail), shifting the middle up about 1.5-2 points vs round 1. The September low is $1,575.15 (close, 09-14), verified on Twelve Data. Research limits: MarketScreener figures are the January-dated consensus page as rendered on 2026-10-01; the FCF/receivables figures came from a search summary of the Q2 IR presentation rather than a direct read.
